summary.title: Code2LoRA: Hypernetwork-Generated Adapters for Code Language Models under Software Evolution

details: Code LMs need repository-level knowledge, but injecting it as long input context (RAG / dependency analysis) costs tokens per query, and per-repository fine-tuning/LoRA is expensive and goes stale as codebases evolve.

Code2LoRA: a hypernetwork that maps a frozen embedding of an entire repository to LoRA weights for a frozen code LM, injecting repository knowledge into parameters with zero inference-time token overhead; only the hypernetwork is trained by the LM loss.

Two instantiations along 'how' vs 'when' knowledge enters: Static directly projects a whole-repository snapshot embedding into LoRA A/B matrices for all seven attention/MLP projection types; Evo maintains a GRU hidden state updated per commit diff embedding that feeds the same LoRA-generation head, yielding an adapter trajectory over the repository's lifetime.

RepoPeftBench: a repository-level PEFT benchmark releasing whole Python repositories (all source files plus commit histories) with assertion-completion tasks, in static-snapshot and commit-history (evolution) tracks.

604 permissively licensed Python repositories using pytest/unittest; 512 in-distribution (>=300 stars, collected before 2025-04-01) and 92 repositories created strictly after that cutoff as temporal OOD holdout.

Task: predict the expected value of an assertion (RHS of comparison or last argument), inspired by LiveCodeBench code execution; input is a structured test-file prefix (imports, enclosing class, helpers, body up to the cut point); non-test code serves as repository context.

Static track: 62K tasks from one snapshot per repo (40K train / 11K val / 12K test). Evolution track: tasks emitted at every assertion-touching commit with the paired production-code diff (215K train / 87K test), capped at <=8 tasks per commit (<=4 per test file at Evo training).
Splits: cross-repo (103 held-out repos) for unseen-codebase generalization and in-repo (409 training repos, chronologically time-segmented on the evolution track).

Base LM: frozen Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B (bf16, 28 layers); repository encoder: frozen Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 4096-token chunks with 512 overlap, mean-pooled per file, then importance-weighted mean concatenated with max pool (2048-dim).
Generated LoRA: rank 16, alpha 32, all seven q/k/v/o/gate/up/down projections, one (A,B) pair shared across all 28 layers, tanh output scaled by learnable log-scales.
~720M trainable parameters (Static) / ~745M (Evo, 1-layer GRU hidden 2048 plus repo-state initializer); truncated BPTT detaching every K=16 commits.
Training: AdamW with cosine schedule, 3 epochs, single H100 80GB; 8K sequence length for Static, 4K for Evo; checkpoint chosen by cross-repo validation loss.
Inference-only: pretrained backbone, RAG (top-k 512-token chunks, k swept), and dependency-resolved context (DRC) built by static import resolution with an adaptive 8K-token budget.
Fine-tuned: full fine-tuning (also FFT+RAG), a single shared LoRA over all repositories, and per-repository LoRA (in-repo upper bound).
Text2LoRA, strengthened to match Code2LoRA on input modality (same whole-repository embedding) and target coverage (all seven projections), so only the LoRA-generation head differs.
Exact Match (relaxed whitespace/punctuation), Edit Similarity (difflib), CodeBLEU.

Analyses: repository-count scaling sweep (10 to 623 training repos), EM vs normalized commit position, per-repository EM variance vs data sparsity, cosine similarity / t-SNE and per-module norms of generated adapters, DRC-availability partition, error taxonomy, and deployment efficiency (tokens, adaptation time, storage).

key_findings.finding: A hypernetwork conditioned on a whole-repository embedding matches per-repository LoRA training while adding zero inference tokens.
key_findings.evidence: On the static track, Code2LoRA-Static reaches 63.8% cross-repo EM (+9.9 pp over the best baseline FFT+RAG at 53.9%; RAG 39.7%, DRC 48.2%, single LoRA 47.4%) and 66.2% in-repo EM versus the 64.0% per-repo LoRA upper bound, with adapter generation under 10 ms and one shared 679 MB hypernetwork instead of 32 MB per repository.

key_findings.finding: Recurrent aggregation of commit diffs is needed once evaluation follows software evolution, where snapshot-based adaptation goes stale.
key_findings.evidence: On commit-derived tasks Code2LoRA-Static drops from 63.8/66.2% to 55.7/60.6% EM (roughly matching single LoRA's 55.1/61.3%), while Code2LoRA-Evo reaches 60.3% cross-repo (+5.2 pp over single LoRA) and 64.5% in-repo, exceeding the 64.2% per-repo LoRA upper bound; the per-commit-position curve shows Evo has the flattest drift while snapshot methods decline fastest.

key_findings.finding: The LoRA-generation head, not input modality or target-module coverage, is the bottleneck for repository-level adaptation.
key_findings.evidence: Text2LoRA strengthened with the identical whole-repository embedding and all seven projection heads, same data/loss/budget, reaches only 45.8% cross-repo EM on the static track (essentially the pretrained 45.7%) and 41.7% on the evolution track, far below Code2LoRA.

key_findings.finding: Context injection can hurt rather than help on this repository-conditioned task, whereas parametric injection is robust.
key_findings.evidence: RAG falls below the pretrained backbone on both tracks and degrades monotonically with k (CR EM 39.7% at k=3 to 36.3% at k=10); DRC gives +1.8 pp over pretrained only on the 70.3% of cross-repo pairs with resolvable imports and is -7.3 pp on the rest, while Code2LoRA-Static is flat across both partitions (67.0 vs 66.9 EM).

key_findings.finding: The hypernetwork emits genuinely repository-specific, structured adapters and gains mainly from repository breadth, which saturates in the low hundreds.
key_findings.evidence: Pairwise cosine similarities of the 52 cross-repo adapters have mean 0.01 (std 0.94) with semantically coherent t-SNE clusters and repo-specific concentration on gate/up projections; cross-repo EM is 57.7% with only 10 training repositories (already above full-data FFT at 51.4%), scales log-linearly to about 200 repos, then flattens; per-repository EM variance is 16.8 (Static) vs 20.9 (per-repo LoRA), which falls below pretrained on 10.5% of repos vs 1.3%.
